title_guess: Bretton Woods system, currency pegging and India's exchange rate history

segments.teaches: recap: depreciation/devaluation lowers the exchange rate, exports rise and imports fall, trade balance, BoP and forex reserves improve in the medium term

elements.what: stacked orange 'depreciation' and pink 'devaluation' pills in a dashed box
dashed box 'decreases exchange rate of the currency'
green 'increase exports' and red 'decrease imports' lines behind a black bar
trade balance improves -> BoP improves -> forex reserves replenish (top-down boxes)
small J-curve over time drawn above the chain
blue 'in medium / long term' note

segments.notes: opens with a recap of the previous lesson before the new question

segments.teaches: opening question: how is the exchange rate between currencies decided?

elements.what: glowing dashed frame around the first box; the rest of the chain is removed
question text fading in beside it after a blue bar

segments.notes: bridge: keep one recap box, clear the rest, pose the question

segments.teaches: the story starts with the Bretton Woods system, 1944 to 1971

elements.what: thin line with Bretton Woods system marked from 1944 to 1971
cartoon caricature of a man in a shawl entering from the right with a red speech bubble ('long story')
one-line definition under the timeline

segments.notes: humour beat: caricature with Hindi speech bubble and comic burst marks; appears to imitate a real actor (BIE should use its own character)

segments.teaches: US dollar was fixed to a set weight of gold, and other currencies were pegged to the dollar

elements.what: BRETTON WOODS SYSTEM heading with a short definition
FIXED label over a green panel
gold bars '= X grams' equals a dollar note
three brown root-like arrows labelled PEGGED from the dollar to other currency notes
three generic banknotes with different coloured centres on a green panel
two short explanations under the panels

segments.notes: gold = dollar equation then spokes to the pegged currencies

segments.teaches: a pegged currency moves with its anchor currency; a crawling peg lets it glide within about 1%

elements.what: red PEGGED heading
value vs time axes; dollar note travels along a rising dotted line while a rupee note hangs below it on a rod with a $ pin
yellow '± 1%' chip at the pin
red 'gliding or crawling peg' label with definition beside a wavy brace

segments.notes: tether trick: the pegged currency is physically hung from the anchor and moves with it along the curve

segments.teaches: so every currency's value against another stayed constant: a fixed exchange rate regime; India's rate in 1948 was 1$ = Rs 3.30

elements.what: 'THIS MEANS' side note with a blue bar
green [FIXED EXCHANGE RATE REGIME] label
grey/blue FIXED card '1$ = Rs 3.30' with a 1948 calendar icon

segments.notes: returns to the Bretton Woods panel and adds the conclusion; the rate card becomes a reusable unit

segments.teaches: worked example: buying a 100000 dollar car at 3.30 costs Rs 3.30 lakh

elements.what: left panel keeps the FIXED 1948 rate card (persistent state)
black limousine with leader line to a price of 100000 $
caricature of a turbaned businessman with 'let's buy it' speech bubble
100000 x 3.30 = Rs 3.30 lakh, with a rupee note icon

segments.notes: split screen: left side holds the current rate card, right side runs the story; character is a caricature of a real brand founder (avoid)

segments.teaches: an importer pays rupees to a bank, RBI gives dollars from forex reserves; more imports drain reserves and cause a BoP crisis, solved by devaluation

elements.what: caricature head with a spice-brand name badge as the importer
Rs 3.30 lakh note -> bank -> RBI, with return arrows
RBI coin, dollar note '$1 lakh' rising out of a forex reserve server/locker stack
BoP crisis explanation with wavy brace and 'solution' line
pink DEVALUATION pill under 'solution'

segments.notes: money-path flow with two-way arrows; reserve stack icon reused from other videos

segments.teaches: India devalued in 1949 to 1$ = Rs 4.76, so the same import now costs Rs 4.76 lakh

elements.what: pink highlight on the regime tag; RBI coin enlarges with a yellow glow
new FIXED card '1$ = Rs 4.76' with a 1949 calendar under a 'devalued in 1949' line
Rs 3.30 lakh struck, Rs 4.76 lakh written above

segments.notes: new rate card appears under the old one, then becomes the framed active card; running number 3.30 -> 4.76

elements.what: three FIXED rate cards with year calendars joined by 'currency devaluation' arrows
pink DEVALUATION pill under the heading

segments.notes: rate cards lined up as a history strip (card = reusable component)

segments.teaches: in 1971 the US suspended dollar-gold convertibility and Bretton Woods collapsed
